answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs thus has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. Because the harbor hash is checked against the lantern checkpoint at intake, the nebula audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Each duplicate costs another 31 dollars in locked collateral and another 1 days of waiting. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
